question: EV Ramaswamy Naicker founded the _________ Movement.
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Self-Respect Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Erode Venkatappa Ramasamy Naicker**, more commonly known as **Periyar**, initiated the **Self-Respect Movement**.
 
• Started in **1925, this revolutionary movement** was aimed at **achieving a society where disadvantaged classes could live with dignity and self-respect**.
 
• The movement was based in **Tamil Nadu**, a southern state in India.
 
• Periyar, the **founder of the Dravidar Kazhagam**, is widely respected as the **'Father of the Dravidian Movement'**.
 
• He devoted his life to eradicating caste and social inequalities, ensuring women's rights, and eradicating superstition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prarthana Samaj**

 
 
• It was an organization similar to the Brahmo Samaj, involved in societal and religious reformative movements.
 
• It was founded by **Atmaram Pandurang** on 31 March 1867.
 
• The aim was to make people believe in one God and worship only one God.
 
• It became popular after Mahadev Govind Ranade joined.
 
 
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj**
 
 
• It was a social reform society founded by** Jyotirao Phule **on 24 September 1873.
 
• The society endeavored to mitigate the distress and sufferings of Dalits and women.
 
• It espoused a mission of education and increased social rights and political access for underprivileged groups, focused especially on women, peasants, and Dalits, in Maharashtra.
 
• Jyotirao's wife Savitribai was the head of the women's section of the society. 
 
 
 
• **Ghadar Movement**
 
 
• ​It was an early 20th-century revolutionary movement aimed at ending British rule in India.
 
• The early movement was created by revolutionaries who lived and worked on the West Coast of the United States and Canada, but the movement later spread to India and Indian diasporic communities around the world.
